clue.text: See gold on its coast: am I going to enter with female title? I've been dead half a century

definitions.text: I've been dead half a century

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: enter tells one piece to go inside the country's name

parts.note: the country whose coast gave gold its name, the old Gold Coast colony
the question 'am I going to?' can be put as 'will I?'
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A rambling travel note about the Gold Coast that ends with a ghostly voice announcing its own half-century in the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghana was the colony called the Gold Coast. The puzzle appeared in August 2008, fifty years after the English composer died in August 1958.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer died in 1958, so at the time of publication he had been dead for fifty years.

clue.text: A lot of shots at netball?

definitions.meaning: a simultaneous discharge of many guns
read as 'at net, ball': a tennis stroke hitting the ball at the net before it bounces

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a burst of gunfire and a stroke played before the ball touches the ground.

clue.text: Greatest possible number among stout characters

indicators.note: among puts the number inside the jumbled letters
the letters of the word are treated as characters to be rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A tally of the most portly figures in some story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' treats the letters of the word as a set to be shuffled, and 'among' places the Roman thousand within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done to the greatest possible degree is done to the fullest extent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Communication job preferably not about Free Enterprise?

definitions.text: Communication job preferably not about Free Enterprise?

parts.words: Communication job preferably not about Free Enterprise?
parts.note: the office of a messenger or announcer, which also reads as the vessel 'Herald of Free Enterprise', the ferry that capsized off Zeebrugge in 1987, so better not to be aboard

explanation.surface: A job in communications that would rather avoid talking about the free market.
explanation.walkthrough: The Herald of Free Enterprise was a British cross-Channel ferry that capsized at Zeebrugge in 1987; 'about' means aboard here, not concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a herald is a job of carrying messages and proclamations, and the phrase also names a ship.

clue.text: Material from vinyl once recorded

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fabric made from old records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded' is a link that finishes the surface picture of gramophone records.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic polymer used as a fabric, so a material in the textile sense.

clue.text: Old instrument making friends with artist

parts.note: kith are one's friends and acquaintances, as in kith and kin
ARA stands for Associate of the Royal Academy, an artist

explanation.surface: An antique instrument that brings friends together with a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek lyre, ancestor of the guitar, so an old instrument.

clue.text: Expression of thanks from variety of solver?

definitions.text: Expression of thanks from variety of solver?

parts.words: Expression of thanks from variety of solver?
parts.note: a polite phrase of gratitude, which read literally describes a 'type' of the person addressed, here the solver

explanation.definitionFit: A courteous phrase of gratitude, which split literally also means a sort or type of the person spoken to.

clue.text: The enemy, time, is on edge

parts.note: a hem is the folded edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Warning that the foe is close at hand and time is running out.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'is on' places T above HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'us and them', the other side is the opposition or enemy.

clue.text: Sailor at airport keeps one from cleansing

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: keeps means the airport holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor detained at an airport is spared from having a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON is a London airport in Bedfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablution is the act of washing oneself, a ritual or everyday cleansing.

clue.text: Trips in a manner are bewildering to the hearer

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something

indicators.note: to the hearer says the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: things that are bewildering daze you

explanation.surface: Journeys that confuse anyone listening to an account of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the hearer' turns DAZE into its sound-alike DAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings, especially away from the workplace or a team's away matches, are trips.

clue.text: Beast to the left, bird to the right

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Directions at a zoo: animal one way, bird the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a Madagascan primate, an animal or beast.

clue.text: Song 1 16 and Nellie composed

indicators.note: composed means the letters are put together afresh, as music is

explanation.surface: A tune written by the composer with a girl called Nellie.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 16' points to the anniversary composer of 1 across/16 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known setting of a William Barnes poem by the composer, so a song of his.

clue.text: Bow bells heard in Cape province?

definitions.meaning: the bells of St Mary-le-Bow ring over the Cockney districts of London
a city in South Africa's old Cape Province, the question mark showing it is a place in the province

explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is traditionally born within sound of Bow bells, in the east of London; a South African port shares the name.

clue.text: Sexy fixer?

parts.note: a fastener such as a shirt or collar fastening, and also a virile man or breeding horse

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses live in one noun, so this is one cryptic phrase rather than two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small fastening device and a sexually active man.

clue.text: Provider of computers with hearts maybe remains in 10

parts.note: Apple is a computer company
the core is the heart or centre of something

explanation.surface: A computer firm with heart, whose leftovers might crop up in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The song at 10 across sings of an apple tree, so the leftovers of eaten fruit might be found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The leftovers after eating the fruit are remains, which might lie under the apple tree of the song.

clue.text: 1 16's s-simple parliamentarian, unpaid and unknown

parts.note: the stammer gives an extra S before a word meaning simple
MP is a Member of Parliament
Hon is short for honorary, an unpaid post
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A stammering account of a simple-minded, unsalaried and obscure MP.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 16's' means a work by the composer of 1 across/16 down: his first symphony, setting Walt Whitman.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's first symphony, a choral setting of Walt Whitman, is one of his works.

clue.text: See 21
See 1 across
Waiter in play, partial tragedy, in returning feature

indicators.note: in puts the part of the tragedy inside the turned feature
returning means the feature is read backwards

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature

indicators.note: partial means only part of the word tragedy is used

explanation.surface: A character in a play, with a hint of tragedy about their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NOSE into ESON; 'partial' takes TRAG from tragedy, and 'in' puts it in the middle. Beckett's play is Waiting for Godot.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two tramps waiting for Godot in Beckett's play, so literally a waiter in a play.

clue.text: August in a cult, possibly not considered

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month, and the puzzle was published in August

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A month spent inside a cult, perhaps without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IN A CULT into INCTUAL. The convention inst. for the current month is used in old commercial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on instinct means acting without deliberation, so not considered.

clue.text: 25 pirate

definitions.meaning: the answer to 25 across can mean of or like ..., from Latin argentum
Long John, the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.definitionFit: The metal is the meaning of the Latinate word at 25, and Long John of that surname is Stevenson's pirate.

clue.text: Sound of charm when with man supplying theme for 1 16

indicators.note: sound of says the word is said aloud

parts.note: a lucky charm is a talisman, so what makes the charm once a man is added is the first part, talis

explanation.surface: A lucky charm and a man together supply the theme for a composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the first part of the word for a lucky charm, the part before 'man', and you hear the Tudor composer whose tune inspired the Fantasia by the composer of 1/16.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor composer wrote the tune for the composer's famous Fantasia on a Theme by him.

clue.text: 1 16's fun when many finish

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, is many
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: The composer had fun when many people finished.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 16's' means a work by the composer at 1 across/16 down: his romance for violin and orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's romance for violin and orchestra, after a George Meredith poem, is a work of his.

clue.text: Continent for 1 16, as in film or akin to 14

definitions.text: Continent for 1 16, as in film or akin to 14

parts.words: Continent for 1 16, as in film or akin to 14
parts.note: the polar continent at the bottom of the globe was the subject of the composer's score for a film about Captain Scott and of the symphony that grew from it, like 14 another symphony

explanation.definitionFit: The polar continent is named directly, and the composer's seventh symphony grew from his music for the film about Scott.

clue.text: Change at noon?

definitions.meaning: noon is where the morning ends, read as AM plus END

explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to change; split up, the word is the end of a.m., which is noon.

clue.text: Monarch with aristocrat as a handle

parts.note: K is short for king
nob is a slang word for a toff or aristocrat

explanation.surface: A king and a nobleman serving as a door handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded handle on a door or drawer is a direct synonym.

clue.text: South American fellow, one embraced by composer

indicators.note: embraced by means the fellow and one go inside the composer

parts.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
a gent is a man or fellow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Latin American man hugged by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an eighteenth-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the country south of Brazil is a South American.

clue.text: Tangle with teacher of 1 16

definitions.meaning: the French composer who taught the composer of 1/16 in Paris in 1908

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to snarl up, and the French composer of Bolero gave lessons to the Englishman.

clue.text: Flood defender on strike, maybe got from …

definitions.text: Flood defender on strike, maybe got from …

parts.words: Flood defender on strike, maybe got from …
parts.note: a sack of sand stacked against floods, which also as a verb means to hit someone, and whose filling might come from the next answer

explanation.definitionFit: A filled sack used to hold back flood water; as a verb it means to strike with such a sack.

clue.text: … what one gets with justice

parts.note: read 'justice' as 'just' plus the thing deserved: the phrase for a fitting punishment is 'just' followed by this word

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 27: the sand in a sandbag may come from arid places, which this word also means.
explanation.definitionFit: One's merited reward or punishment, as in getting one's just reward, which the clue splits out of 'justice'.
